page_note: Heavily damaged page (100% damage ratio) preserving fragments of an anti-monist polemical argument: against opponents who hold 'there is one substance' / 'no other existing besides God'. The argument runs dialectically — listing evils (lie, false witness, slander, magic, adultery, theft, idolatry, sorcery, fornication, Mammon-greed) and challenging: if God established all, where do these come from? Closes with reference to 'his beloved Son' proclaiming the evil ones are 'the Evil One' (ⲡⲡⲟⲛⲏⲣⲟⲥ). This is classic Manichaean dualist polemic against Zoroastrian/Jewish/Christian monism — not correspondential substrate. The vice-list is rhetorical accusation, not cosmic mapping. No segments preserve the older teaching layer; the entire page is editorial polemic. Heavy editorial fatigue drift (+4.7 toward polemic in second half) confirms the polemical character.
